expectations.text: Output contains a mechanical identity / decomposition section identifying the three-pool balancing and transfer cost as core mechanics
expectations.evidence: Has 'The Core Mechanic, Interpreted' (3 sentences) but no structured decomposition of loops, resource dynamics, tension structure etc. Transfer cost is acknowledged ('can be fed into each other at a cost') but not analyzed as a mechanical pillar.

expectations.text: At least 5 distinct setting concepts are presented
expectations.evidence: Exactly 5 settings: Dying Space Station, Medieval Kingdom in Decline, Research Outpost, Underground City, Long-Haul Cargo Ship.

expectations.text: Each setting's three pools correspond to three specific named things in the fiction that make intuitive sense
expectations.evidence: All 5 settings: Space Station (Oxygen/Power/Structural Integrity), Kingdom (Food/Morale/Order), Research Outpost (Data Integrity/Equipment Condition/Researcher Wellbeing), Underground City (Air Quality/Social Cohesion/Infrastructure), Cargo Ship (Fuel/Crew Readiness/Cargo Integrity). All intuitive.

expectations.text: At least 2 settings include specific diegetic or semi-diegetic UI concepts for the three pools
expectations.evidence: No UI/UX Hooks sections in any setting. Recommendations vaguely mention 'an obvious visual language (gauges, readouts, facility maps)' but without specifics. No setting suggests a concrete diegetic UI approach.

expectations.text: No setting demands high-fidelity 3D animation, complex physics, or real-time action systems
expectations.evidence: All settings are appropriate for browser idle. Recommendations explicitly note: 'Both have an obvious visual language (gauges, readouts, facility maps)' — all 2D/flat appropriate.

expectations.text: At least 3 settings' Mechanical Mappings explain why transferring between the three things costs something in the fiction
expectations.evidence: The 'Cross-Cutting Design Considerations' section addresses this for all settings: 'The cost of transfer should be visible and interpretable.' Individual settings also address it: Space Station ('rerouting power to oxygen scrubbers strains the hull'), Kingdom ('taxing the peasants raises Order but destroys Morale'). The principle section is good but per-setting specificity is inconsistent.

expectations.text: At least one setting frames the accelerating drain as something that makes thematic sense, not just a difficulty curve
expectations.evidence: The 'Cross-Cutting Design Considerations' section: 'The accelerating drain should have a narrative explanation... If it's cascading system failure, political instability compounding, equipment wearing faster because it's already worn — the player feels like they're losing for reasons they understand.' Space Station description: 'cascading system failure' explained. Kingdom: 'political instability compounding'.

notes: Without the skill, the baseline hit 4/7 assertions. It generated 5 good settings with correct pool naming, and the Cross-Cutting Design Considerations section showed strong design thinking. Main gaps: no structured mechanical decomposition, no UI/UX hooks. The baseline favors breadth (5 settings) over depth (missing structure).
